title: vocabularies.match
description: Resolve ONE free-text guess to ONE term code, with a score, or refuse. This object validates the request payload; the response is the two-shaped answer in $defs.Match. The caller is not a keyboard — it is a composer in another service holding a string it got out of a photo, a title or a language model, and whatever comes back is written into a listing with no human in between. So this is not a search: a search may answer loosely because a person reads five rows and picks. Here a wrong code is silently wrong data and a refusal costs one clarifying question, which is why every candidate is scored against a floor and everything under it comes back matched:false. The ladder is exact (1.0), unique prefix (0.9), then the vector seam, which returns the similarity the far side actually stated — an unscored answer is refused rather than assigned a number.

text.description: The free-text guess — a label in any script, or a code. Whitespace is trimmed.

parent.description: When given, only children of this term are candidates — the same parentage rule vocabularies.resolve applies (a Color under a Model, a Model under a Vendor). A parent naming no term matches nothing rather than falling back to the whole level.

min_score.description: Floor for this call, overriding STAPEL_VOCABULARIES['MATCH_MIN_SCORE'] (default 0.8). Raise it where a wrong value is expensive, lower it where a human still confirms the answer.

Match.description: The response. Exactly two shapes, and `matched` is which: a hit carries code/label/score/method, a miss carries only a reason. There is deliberately no third shape holding a low-confidence guess.

code.description: The matched term's code, on a hit. This is the value a listing stores.

label.description: The matched term's label, on a hit — so the caller can show a human what it decided.

score.description: Confidence, on a hit: 1.0 for an exact hit on a folded label or on a code, 0.9 for a UNIQUE prefix hit, and for a vector hit the similarity the underlying Function stated, verbatim. Never a number this module invented.

method.description: Which rung answered. Worth logging: a deployment where everything arrives by `vector` is one whose catalogue labels do not match how its sellers write.

reason.description: Why there is no answer, on a miss. `no_confident_match` covers every 'the question was well formed and nothing cleared the floor' case — including an ambiguous prefix, a parent that scopes everything out, an unconfigured or unreachable vector seam, and a neighbour returned without a score.
